text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 7.4% today, erasing most of yesterday's 2.9% rebound and reaching a two-week low. The drop came as oil prices ticked higher on Middle East supply concerns from Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries, but the company's refining margins appear squeezed by a mismatch in what refiners can earn: U.S. crude costs $107.89 per barrel while refined products (gasoline and diesel) sit in ample storage at 205 and 104 million barrels respectively. When refiners have too much product relative to demand and crude costs rise, their profit per gallon of output shrinks.

The broader headwind is the geopolitical whipsaw—oil prices swung on conflicting signals about Iran war resolution through the week, creating uncertainty for refiners trying to plan operations. At 93.4% utilization, refineries are already running hot, leaving little room to ramp up production if margins improve. The Trump administration's potential move to allow Russian diesel into U.S. markets adds another layer of downward pressure on refined fuel pricing, which directly hits refiner profitability.
